short.q: Describe the difference between an acciaccatura and an appoggiatura.
short.model: An acciaccatura is a very short crushed note; an appoggiatura is a longer leaning note that takes part of the main note's value.
It moves mostly by step to adjacent notes, giving a smooth, singable line.

short.q: How do you find the relative minor of a major key?
short.model: Go down a minor third (three semitones) from the tonic; it shares the key signature.

short.q: Name and describe a melodic device where a phrase repeats at a different pitch.
short.model: A sequence: the motif is repeated higher or lower, often stepwise.

short.q: Why is the blues scale used in blues and rock?
short.model: It contains blue notes (flattened fifth), giving the characteristic bent, expressive sound.
